welcome_message:
Monitoring SQL Warehouse: Asset Installer

Installs a single Declarative Automation Bundle resource file that
defines a small, dedicated serverless SQL warehouse tuned for bursty
workloads (scheduled Databricks Alerts, monitoring queries, ad-hoc
health checks).

Why it exists: Alerts and monitoring queries are sub-second, but a
general-purpose warehouse on a long auto-stop window stays warm for
minutes after each run. Idle time dominates the bill. A dedicated
2X-Small serverless warehouse with auto_stop_mins=1 keeps the cost
proportional to actual query time.

The asset is opinionated about serverless PRO: the 1-minute auto-stop
is only valid on serverless. Pro/Classic stay at the 10-minute floor.

Let's pick the install settings...

target_dir.description:
Target directory for the warehouse resource file (relative to your bundle root).
Most bundles already include `resources/*.yml` from databricks.yml, so the
default `resources` lands the file where the bundle will auto-pick it up.

If your bundle uses a different convention (e.g., `resources/sql_warehouses/`),
set that here. The directory will be created if it does not exist.
target_dir
target_dir.pattern_match_failure_message: Target directory must start with a letter, number, or underscore and contain only letters, numbers, underscores, slashes, hyphens, or dots.

warehouse_resource_key.description:
========================================

DABs resource key for the warehouse.

This key appears in the bundle as `resources.sql_warehouses.<key>` and is
also the filename: `<target_dir>/<key>.sql_warehouse.yml`. Other bundle
resources reference this warehouse by `${resources.sql_warehouses.<key>.id}`.

Default `monitoring_sql_warehouse` is safe for most projects. Pick another
name only if your bundle already defines a warehouse with this key.
Must be lowercase snake_case (letters, numbers, underscores).
warehouse_resource_key
warehouse_resource_key.pattern_match_failure_message: Resource key must be lowercase, start with a letter, and contain only letters, numbers, and underscores.

warehouse_name.description:
========================================

Display name shown in the Databricks workspace SQL Warehouses list.

This is what users see in the UI when picking a warehouse for an Alert
or query. Free-form; spaces and mixed case are fine.
warehouse_name

cluster_size.description:
========================================

Cluster size for the warehouse.

Valid Databricks SQL warehouse sizes (smallest to largest):
  2X-Small, X-Small, Small, Medium, Large, X-Large, 2X-Large, 3X-Large, 4X-Large, 5X-Large

Default `2X-Small` is the smallest and cheapest. It is sufficient for
Databricks Alerts and monitoring queries that complete in under a second.
Scale up only if your queries scan large tables.
cluster_size
cluster_size.pattern_match_failure_message: Cluster size must be one of: 2X-Small, X-Small, Small, Medium, Large, X-Large, 2X-Large, 3X-Large, 4X-Large, 5X-Large.

auto_stop_mins.description:
========================================

Idle minutes before the warehouse auto-stops (integer).

Default `1` is the serverless minimum verified via DABs deploy: the UI
shows 'After 1 minute of inactivity'. Sub-minute values are NOT supported
(the field is modeled as an integer).

Special values:
  0  = disable auto-stop entirely (warehouse runs until manually stopped)
  1  = serverless minimum (recommended for Alerts / bursty workloads)
  10+ = required floor for Pro/Classic warehouses; safe upper bound for serverless too

Keep at 1 unless you have a reason to override.
auto_stop_mins
auto_stop_mins.pattern_match_failure_message: auto_stop_mins must be a non-negative integer (0 to disable, 1 for serverless minimum, 10+ for Pro/Classic).

success_message:
========================================

Monitoring SQL warehouse installed:
  - Resource:  {{.target_dir}}/{{.warehouse_resource_key}}.sql_warehouse.yml
  - Usage doc: docs/monitoring-sql-warehouse/README.md

Next steps:

1. Confirm your `databricks.yml` includes the resource file. Most bundles
   already include `resources/*.yml` by default; verify:
     include:
       - resources/*.yml
   If you installed to a custom subdirectory, add the matching glob.

2. Validate and deploy:
     databricks bundle validate -t <your-target>
     databricks bundle deploy -t <your-target>

3. After deploy, the warehouse appears in the workspace SQL Warehouses list
   as '{{.warehouse_name}}'. Point your Alerts / monitoring queries at it.

4. Reference the warehouse ID from other bundle resources via:
     ${resources.sql_warehouses.{{.warehouse_resource_key}}.id}

Usage notes, the auto_stop_mins=1 nuance, and the CLI/API paths for
existing warehouses live in 'docs/monitoring-sql-warehouse/README.md'.
